Firm | August 15, 2022 Global law firm Norton Rose Fulbright today announced that seven lawyers, including partners John F. Young and Christine Fernandez Owen , and three paralegals have joined its real estate practice . The team previously comprised Clean Law PC, a Chicago-based boutique renewables real estate firm representing leading and emerging developers and operators of clean energy projects in the United States and globally. Along with partners Young and Fernandez Owen, the projects-focused real estate team includes counsel Kacie Bevers, Kayce Kasten Borders , Theresa Carroll, Damola Omisore and Lauren Shapiro as well as senior paralegal Kathy Wenger and paralegals Ali Berry and Kelsei Peppler. Young, Fernandez Owen, Borders, Carroll, Berry and Peppler all join the Chicago office. Bevers and Omisore will be based in Houston , with Shapiro in Austin and Wenger in Minneapolis . Jeff Cody , Norton Rose Fulbright s US Managing Partner, said: Projects and real estate are two cornerstones of Norton Rose Fulbright s business practice, which we have prioritized as a growth area for the firm. I am pleased to welcome John, Christine and the rest of this dynamic team as we continue our commitment to bringing on top talent dedicated to excellence in client service. Daniel Farris, Norton Rose Fulbright s Chicago Partner-in-Charge, said: We are thrilled to welcome John, Christine and their team to Norton Rose Fulbright s growing Chicago office, which has as a mainstay innovation and next generation technology in all of the key industries. With hundreds of lawyers focused on renewable energy across the firm, this forward-thinking team further strengthens our position as leaders in this space. Young advises renewable energy developers and operators on an extensive array of real estate and other matters. He previously served as in-house counsel to a global renewable energy developer where he was responsible for handling all legal aspects of the company s North American real estate development, as well as serving as primary counsel for Department of Defense initiatives. Young has experience with joint venture relationships, project acquisition and divestiture, construction projects, purchasing/supply chain master service arrangements, corporate governance issues and compliance matters. Young, who founded Clean Law PC in 2017, said: I am delighted to join Norton Rose Fulbright, which advises on some of the most significant real estate and projects deals in the world. My team and our clients will benefit from the firm s talented legal practitioners as well as its unmatched global reach and roster of projects clients. Fernandez Owen provides legal services to developers, owners and operators of wind, solar and energy storage projects. Her practice is focused on the support of development efforts of renewable projects, including negotiation of site control documents, title and other real estate review, environmental diligence, negotiation of commercial contracts used in the development and construction of renewable energy projects, and diligence in support of acquisitions and financing of renewable energy projects. Prior to private practice, Fernandez Owen was assistant general counsel at one of the world s largest developers and owners of renewable energy projects, where she also worked as a wind developer. Fernandez Owen, who has more than 13 years of experience in the renewable energy industry, said: The clean energy market is booming, and our team has been at the forefront of its evolution with our clients. I am excited to join Norton Rose Fulbright s premier real estate team and collaborate with its projects practice group, which is widely recognized as the best by clients and industry experts. Norton Rose Fulbright has more than 200 real estate lawyers globally advising clients across the full range of real estate matters, including urban regeneration projects, direct and indirect investment transactions, real estate financing, equity investment structuring, portfolio deals, corporate occupier matters, dispute resolution and development projects. The firm has more than 220 projects lawyers around the globe acting on some of the world s most innovative, complex and challenging deals. Norton Rose Fulbright sees a large share of the project finance market. In the last four years, the firm s projects lawyers advised on more than 400 significant transactions with a total value of more than $200 billion (IJGlobal Q3, 2022). On April 12, Norton Rose Fulbright announced the opening of its Chicago office, with the firm becoming the first major law firm to establish its home base in the vibrant Fulton Market District. The firm s 12 th US location and 53 rd office worldwide opened with 11 lawyers serving tech and tech-enabled businesses in transformative sectors across a range of practices, including projects, employment and labor, technology transactions, intellectual property and privacy and data security. Prepare yourself for a journey where ambitions align with action, innovations transform industries, and the futur ETRetail Newsletters Explore and Subscribe to our Daily Newsletters Follow Us Get updates of events and latest news from ETRetail on LinkedIn Food Services 1 min Read 10on10 Foods starts work on second Bengaluru unit, raises monthly capacity fivefold to 1,200 tonnes “The new unit gives us the ability to do two important things — deliver against the demand we are receiving and incorporate technology that allows us to launch newer and better-quality products,” said Ashish Bajaj, CEO and co-founder, 10on10 Foods. E ETRetail Desk ETRetail Published On Sep 09, 2026 at 12:30 PM IST Set ETRetail as your preferred source on Google Share Icon Copy Link Share on Whatsapp Share on Linkedin Share on X Share on Telegram Share on Facebook Bookmark Comment Fresh staples brand 10on10 Foods has started work on its second manufacturing unit in Bengaluru , increasing its monthly production capacity in the city from 200 tonnes to 1,200 tonnes. Milling operations at the new facility are expected to begin within 50-60 days. The expansion comes within eight months of the company starting operations and is aimed at meeting growing demand while adding capacity for technology-led improvements in milling and product development. The company said the facility will allow it to introduce new processes aimed at improving milling efficiency and the nutritional value of its products. The new unit gives us the ability to do two important things deliver against the demand we are receiving and incorporate technology that allows us to launch newer and better-quality products, said Ashish Bajaj, CEO and co-founder, 10on10 Foods. The company is also expanding its distribution and manufacturing footprint. It is working with a quick-commerce player on the exclusive launch of new products and plans to establish manufacturing facilities in Mumbai and Hyderabad in the coming months. With the additional Bengaluru capacity, 10on10 Foods is targeting fivefold growth by FY27. Founded in Bengaluru, 10on10 Foods offers freshly milled atta, millet-based products including jowar, bajra and ragi variants, and high-protein staples through its omnichannel and quick-commerce network. This is a key position within our Texas operation. We are looking for someone who is not only a strong estimator, but who can help lead and develop a team of estimators while ensuring our estimating process is accurate, efficient, organized, and responsive to our customers. The Senior Estimator will work closely with our sales, estimating, and operations teams from initial bid opportunity through project handoff. This person must be comfortable managing multiple priorities, reviewing complex plans and specifications, assisting with RFIs and submittals, and ensuring proposals are complete, concise, and accurately reflect the project scope. Key Responsibilities Lead, support, and help develop a team of estimators. Prepare accurate and competitive estimates for commercial roofing and related scopes. Review plans, specifications, addenda, and other contract documents to identify complete project requirements. Perform detailed quantity takeoffs and develop labor, material, equipment, and subcontractor costs. Review estimates prepared by other team members for accuracy, completeness, and consistency. Work efficiently through multiple bid opportunities while meeting customer and internal deadlines. Prepare clear, concise, and professional proposals that accurately define scope, inclusions, exclusions, and qualifications. Assist with RFIs, submittals, product information, and other preconstruction requirements. Work closely with the sales team to evaluate opportunities, clarify scope, develop pricing strategies, and respond to customer questions. Identify scope gaps, potential risks, constructability concerns, and opportunities before projects are contracted. Participate in project handoffs to operations and communicate the assumptions and details behind the estimate. Help establish and maintain consistent estimating standards, processes, and accountability within the San Marcos team. Roofing & Exterior Scope Experience Candidates should have strong knowledge of commercial construction and experience estimating multiple roofing and exterior systems, including: TPO and other single-ply roofing systems Shingle roofing Standing seam and other metal roofing systems Metal wall panels Soffit and fascia Gutters and related sheet metal Insulation, cover board, flashings, accessories, and associated roofing components Qualifications Minimum 5 years of commercial roofing estimating experience. Strong understanding of commercial roofing systems, installation methods, materials, and specifications. Ability to read and interpret architectural drawings, specifications, details, and contract documents. Proven ability to produce accurate takeoffs, estimates, and proposals. Strong organizational skills with the ability to manage multiple bids and deadlines simultaneously. Excellent verbal and written communication skills. Ability to communicate effectively with customers, general contractors, manufacturers, salespeople, estimators, and operations personnel. Strong attention to detail and commitment to accuracy. Comfortable taking ownership of problems and driving them through resolution. Leadership or management experience is preferred. Ability and willingness to coach, train, and develop other estimators is highly valued. What We Are Looking For The right person for this position is more than an experienced estimator. We are looking for someone who can help strengthen our entire estimating operation in Texas. This person should be able to lead while still doing the work. Someone who can review a difficult set of plans, help another estimator work through a problem, communicate directly with a customer or salesperson, and keep the team moving toward deadlines. Success in this position means producing accurate work, communicating clearly, developing the people around you, and helping d-7 Roofing pursue the right projects with the right scope and pricing. Nobody has opened it since the day it was set up, or the owner has it bookmarked and reads the average position column like a league table, twice a day, worrying about a number that moves for reasons they cannot influence. Table of Contents Toggle What Search Console Is, and Who It Is For What it reports on, and what it cannot see Why it is not Google Analytics Setting It Up Properly on a WordPress Site Domain property versus URL prefix Verifying ownership and adding users The Five Reports Worth Your Attention Performance: queries, pages and countries Page Indexing: what the states really mean Sitemaps, Core Web Vitals and Links Reading the Performance Report Without Panicking Clicks, impressions, CTR and average position Why your rank tracking tool disagrees with Google Diagnosing a Page That Will Not Index URL Inspection and the live test Requesting indexing the right way Alerts, Manual Actions and Security Issues A Monthly 20 Minute Routine The three questions to answer each month What to export and keep Mistakes That Make Search Console Useless What to Do When the Numbers Fall Search Console FAQ Do I need Search Console if my developer already set it up? How often should I check it? Why does my position look worse in Search Console than in my rank tracker? What does it mean when a page says it is discovered but not indexed? Can Search Console tell me if I have been penalised? What should I export and keep? Get a free consultation with us Both are easy to understand. It is free, it is the only place Google reports its own data about your site, and it becomes genuinely useful once you know which four or five screens matter and what the numbers cannot tell you. After 13 years of working with it, my view has settled. Google Search Console is a diagnostic instrument, not a scoreboard, and most of it can be ignored most weeks. What follows is what to set up, what to read, what to leave alone, and a monthly routine that takes about twenty minutes. What Search Console Is, and Who It Is For What it reports on, and what it cannot see Google describes the service in one line: "Search Console provides information on how Google crawls, indexes, and serves websites." That framing tells you which questions the tool can answer. Whether a page is indexed. Whether Google hit an error fetching it. Which queries returned your pages in results. Whether any manual action or security problem exists. What it cannot see is everything that happens after the click. No revenue, no form submissions, no behaviour on the page, no attribution. Those are analytics questions, and expecting search reports to answer them is the root of most disappointment with the tool. Why it is not Google Analytics The two get confused at least once in every project. Search Console reports on Google's side of the transaction: what it crawled, what it kept, and what it served for which query. Analytics reports on your side: what happened after someone arrived. One tells you whether you were shown, the other tells you what the visit was worth. Setting It Up Properly on a WordPress Site Domain property versus URL prefix A domain property covers every version of your site: secure and unsecured, www and non www, and every subdomain. A URL prefix property covers one address pattern only. Choose the domain property. Otherwise half your reporting lives somewhere else and you spend a month wondering why part of the site is missing from the numbers. Verifying ownership and adding users Verification through a DNS record or an uploaded file both work, and the choice matters less than who holds access afterwards. Ask for your own user with full permission. If a developer or agency holds the only verified property and you have no login, fixing that is the first task, ahead of any reporting question. The Five Reports Worth Your Attention Performance: queries, pages and countries The Performance report shows what your pages were served for, and Google describes the default window plainly: "The default view of the report shows click and impression data for your site in Google Search results for the past three months." Read it by query first, then by page, then narrow the date range when you want to investigate something specific. Page Indexing: what the states really mean The Page Indexing report groups addresses by state: indexed, crawled but not indexed, discovered but not indexed, alternate page with a proper canonical, and several more. Read the states as a queue of decisions running from discovery down to confirmation. A page sitting in discovered but not indexed has a different problem from one sitting in crawled but not indexed, and the fixes are not interchangeable. Sitemaps, Core Web Vitals and Links The remaining reports are useful on the days you need them and quiet the rest of the time. Sitemaps tells you whether the file was read and how many addresses were accepted. Core Web Vitals groups page experience problems. Links shows what Google sees pointing at your site, internal and external, which is occasionally revealing when an internal link you expected is not being counted. Reading the Performance Report Without Panicking Clicks, impressions, CTR and average position Four numbers and one habit. Clicks are visits from search. Impressions are how often you appeared. The ratio between them is your click through rate. Average position is the mean rank of your topmost result across every query and location where you appeared, which is why it can look worse in a month when traffic actually grew. Why your rank tracking tool disagrees with Google Because they measure different things. Google explains one reason clearly: "Even if a query appears in your list, you might not see your site in results if you run the same query in Google Search. This is because Search results are specific to the time, place, device, and recent history of the person searching." A rank tracker checks one query, from one location, on a schedule. Treat the two as instruments rather than verdicts. The full detail sits on the Performance report help page . Diagnosing a Page That Will Not Index URL Inspection and the live test URL Inspection is the workhorse. Google describes it as the tool that "provides information about Google's indexed version of a specific page, and also allows you to test whether a URL might be indexable." Use the live test after a fix, so you are comparing against what exists now rather than what Google last saw. Requesting indexing the right way One request after a real change, then patience. Google also names the limit of the tool: "The URL Inspection tool doesn't take into account all requirements for appearing on Google." A page can be perfectly indexable and still never appear for the query you care about, because indexability and relevance are separate tests. Both are covered on the URL Inspection help page . Alerts, Manual Actions and Security Issues Check these three on your first visit and monthly afterwards. Manual actions are rare and always explicit, naming the reason and the affected section. Security issues flag hacked content, malicious redirects and unwanted software, and they are worth acting on the day they appear. Beyond the reports, Search Console sends email when it finds something, and those messages are one of the few notifications from Google worth keeping switched on. Both reports are the definitive answer to the question owners ask most often after a bad month. If a penalty exists, it appears here with a description. If nothing appears here, the cause is elsewhere. A Monthly 20 Minute Routine The three questions to answer each month Did more of the right people find us, judged by clicks and impressions on the queries that matter commercially. Did anything break, judged by the Page Indexing report and the error counts. And what changed, judged by comparing this month with the same month last year rather than with last month. Those three questions take less time than scrolling the interface randomly, and they produce a decision rather than a feeling. What to export and keep Export the Performance report by query and by page, and note the indexed and excluded address counts. The interface keeps a limited window, so two or three quarters of exported history is the only dependable way to tell whether a change helped. Once you have that export habit, the next step is usually joining it to the behaviour data, which is when you need the analytics layer as well . Mistakes That Make Search Console Useless Four mistakes do most of the damage. Checking daily and reacting to incomplete data. Reading average position as a score rather than an average. Comparing a thirty day period with a ninety day period and drawing a conclusion. And treating the tool as a submission queue rather than a report. Google's own advice on frequency is the plainest sentence in the documentation: "There is no need to sign in to the tool every day." Its guidance adds that a monthly check, or a check after site changes, is enough. One more fact catches people out. The removals tool is temporary rather than permanent, because "a successful request lasts only about six months, to allow time for you to find a solution to either allow the content to be seen or to remove it permanently." If you need a page gone for good, the temporary request is not the mechanism. The whole picture is on Google's page about getting started with Search Console . What to Do When the Numbers Fall Work through a short order. Check Manual Actions and Security Issues first, because they are definitive. Then check the Page Indexing report for a fall in indexed addresses. Then check whether an address pattern changed, including a redirect that stopped resolving or a template edit that added a noindex instruction. Then look at the queries themselves, because a fall in brand queries and a fall in non brand queries mean different things. If the reports are clean and the queries moved, the cause is usually competitive or intent related rather than technical. Two habits make all of this quicker. Keep the technical SEO checklist this feeds into beside the account, and read the reports with a consultant to read it with you at least once a quarter. If you are starting from scratch, the questions owners ask about Search Console cover the setup problems that come up most. Search Console FAQ Do I need Search Console if my developer already set it up? Yes, and you should hold your own access. Google describes it as a free service that helps you monitor, maintain and troubleshoot your site's presence in search, and it is the only place that reports Google's own data about your property. If your developer or agency owns the only verified property, ask to be added before anything else happens. How often should I check it? Google's own guidance is that there is no need to sign in every day, and that a monthly check, or a check after site changes, is enough. Weekly is reasonable if you are publishing actively. Daily checking mostly produces worry, because the newest data is incomplete and average position moves for reasons outside your control. Why does my position look worse in Search Console than in my rank tracker? Because they measure different things. Average position in Search Console is the average position of your topmost result across many queries and many searchers, and Google notes that results are specific to the time, place, device and recent history of the person searching. A rank tracker checks one query from one location on a schedule. Treat them as two instruments, not two verdicts. What does it mean when a page says it is discovered but not indexed? It means Google knows the address exists and has chosen not to index it yet, or has not got to it. The usual causes are quality, duplication, thin content or a crawl decision rather than a technical block. Check for a self referencing canonical, confirm the page is linked internally, and improve the page rather than requesting indexing repeatedly. Can Search Console tell me if I have been penalised? For manual actions, yes. The Manual Actions report shows whether Google has applied one and where. It cannot show algorithmic ranking changes, which appear as gradual or abrupt declines with no notification. If traffic falls and the Manual Actions and Security Issues reports are clean, the cause is usually competitive or intent related. What should I export and keep? Keep a monthly export of the Performance report by query and by page, and a monthly count of indexed versus excluded addresses. Over two or three quarters that history is the only dependable way to tell whether a change helped, because the interface keeps only a limited window and comparisons get muddled by seasonality. September 2026 Mitgründer von mika: Henry Müssemann, Agnieszka Walorska, Luke Linnekuhle | © Beto Ruiz Alonso Das Berliner FinTech mika hat sechs Millionen Euro in einer Seed-Finanzierungsrunde eingesammelt. Angeführt wird die Runde vom europäischen Investor Smedvig Ventures. Außerdem beteiligen sich Wecken & Cie., die studiVZ-Mitgründer Dennis Bemmann und Michael Brehm, limango-Gründer Johannes Ditterich sowie Martina Pfeifer von encourageventures. Die Bestandsinvestoren Keen Venture Partners und Dutch Founders Fund erhöhen ihre Beteiligungen. Das Kapital soll in das weitere Wachstum und die Entwicklung des KI-Systems fließen. KI-native Alternative zum Steuerbüro mika will nicht lediglich bestehende Prozesse von Steuerkanzleien digitalisieren. Stattdessen baut das Startup Buchhaltung und steuerliche Prozesse für kleine Unternehmen von Grund auf rund um künstliche Intelligenz auf. Das Angebot richtet sich insbesondere an kleine GmbHs und UGs. Für diese übernimmt mika unter anderem die laufende Buchhaltung, Umsatzsteuervoranmeldungen, Jahresabschlüsse und Steuererklärungen. Das Herzstück bildet ein KI-natives Hauptbuch. Je nach Aufgabe kommen unterschiedliche KI-Modelle zum Einsatz, die mit selbst entwickelten Regeln und Fachwissen kombiniert werden. Die Software verarbeitet Belege und Zahlungen, nimmt Zuordnungen und Buchungen vor und soll Nutzern zugleich erklären können, was die jeweiligen Vorgänge für ihr Unternehmen bedeuten. Menschen bleiben Teil des Systems Vollständig auf menschliche Expertise verzichtet mika dabei nicht. Ausgebildete Buchhalter im Unternehmen überprüfen Ergebnisse und übernehmen Fälle, bei denen zusätzliche menschliche Bearbeitung erforderlich ist. Eine individuelle Steuerberatung gehört bislang nicht zum Angebot. Für entsprechende Fragestellungen arbeitet mika mit zugelassenen Steuerberatern aus einem Partnernetzwerk zusammen. Darüber hinaus setzt das Unternehmen auf einen KI-Chat. Nutzer können beispielsweise Schreiben des Finanzamts hochladen und sich deren Inhalt sowie notwendige nächste Schritte erklären lassen. Auch Fragen zu den eigenen Unternehmenszahlen sollen sich direkt über mika stellen lassen. Über das Model Context Protocol (MCP) können Daten zudem in KI-Assistenten wie ChatGPT oder Claude eingebunden werden. Mehr als 750 Unternehmen nutzen mika Das Unternehmen kann bereits eine deutliche kommerzielle Traktion vorweisen. Zu Jahresbeginn nutzten rund 400 GmbHs und UGs das Angebot, mittlerweile sind es nach Unternehmensangaben mehr als 750. Gestartet ist mika vor allem bei digital arbeitenden Dienstleistern wie Agenturen und Beratungen. Mittlerweile kommen Kunden aus Bereichen wie SaaS, Immobilien und E-Commerce hinzu. Zuletzt habe das Startup auch Unternehmen aus Einzelhandel und Handwerk gewonnen. Der Umsatz wächst laut mika seit mehreren Monaten um mehr als 20 Prozent pro Monat. Im Juli 2026 überschritt das Unternehmen die Marke von einer Million Euro Jahresumsatz. Smedvig Ventures führt Seed-Runde an Mit Smedvig Ventures gewinnt mika einen neuen Lead-Investor. Der Londoner VC investiert europaweit in B2B-Technologieunternehmen in der Seed- und Series-A-Phase. Hinter mika stehen CEO Agnieszka Walorska, CFO Luke Linnekuhle und CTO Henry Müssemann. Linnekuhle war zuvor am Aufbau des Finanzbereichs von Oceansapart beteiligt. Müssemann arbeitete als Head of Engineering beim Softwareunternehmen Freezingdata, das später verkauft wurde. SaaS für Buchhaltung und Steuern mika positioniert sich damit in einer wachsenden Kategorie KI-nativer Dienstleistungsunternehmen. Statt Software bereitzustellen, mit der Menschen bestehende Dienstleistungen effizienter erledigen, soll die Technologie zunehmend Teile der Dienstleistung selbst übernehmen. Gerade der deutsche Steuer- und Buchhaltungsmarkt bietet dafür aufgrund seiner Komplexität ein interessantes, aber anspruchsvolles Umfeld. Gleichzeitig muss mika zeigen, dass sich die Kombination aus KI-Automatisierung und menschlicher Kontrolle auch bei steigender Kundenzahl zuverlässig skalieren lässt. Die bisherigen Wachstumszahlen liefern dafür erste Anhaltspunkte. Mit den zusätzlichen sechs Millionen Euro kann mika nun versuchen, aus der KI-Buchhaltung für kleine Kapitalgesellschaften eine breiter skalierbare Alternative zu klassischen Strukturen aufzubauen.
